ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s fleeing audience has an indicated underlying motive; the Prophet should ignore them and only remind them, while benefit is reserved for those God’s laws make receptive.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r4.claim: Disbelievers demand open scrolls individually as an excuse; 6:124 records a similar demand to receive what God's prophets received, while God knows whom to entrust.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p58/r4.anchor: why were not open scrolls handed to each one of them

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r1.speaker: الجمهور وابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r1.claim: The majority read suhufan with both letters rounded; Ibn Jubayr reads both with sukun and uses the lighter form of munashshara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: صحفا بضم الصاد والحاء، منشرة مشددا وابن جبير: بإسكانها منشرة مخففا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r2.claim: Munashshara likens spreading a page to God reviving the dead; for the dead one says God revived him and he lived.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p340/r2.anchor: شبه نشر الصحيفة بإنشار الله الموتى

MUQATIL:74:34-52/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r10.claim: Meccan unbelievers demanded a revealed, individual written scripture proving their idols false, God's truth, Muhammad's mission, and angelic testimony; Gabriel offered to punish them like Israel, but the Prophet disliked this, and God says they will not believe the requested books.
MUQATIL:74:34-52/r10.anchor: { بل يريد كل امرىء منهم أن يؤتى }

TABRISI:74:32-56/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:32-56/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:74:32-56/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr's anomalous reading has the ḥāʾ and nūn unvoweled in ‘spread-out pages.’
TABRISI:74:32-56/r4.anchor: وقراءة سعيد بن جبير صحفا منشرة بسكون الحاء والنون

TABRISI:74:32-56/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:32-56/r13.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:74:32-56/r13.claim: Sukun on the ḥāʾ in ṣuḥuf is a Tamim dialect; the sukun in munshara is justified by common use of nashara cloth and God raising the dead, though the alternative verb is also attested.
TABRISI:74:32-56/r13.anchor: قال ابن جني: أما سكون الحاء من صحف فلغة تميمية وأما منشرة بسكون النون فإن العرف في الاستعمال نشرت الثوب

TABRISI:74:32-56/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:32-56/r14.speaker: المتنبي
TABRISI:74:32-56/r14.claim: Al-Mutanabbi's ‘made alive’ line witnesses using ‘spread’ for revived, permitting analogy between a revived corpse and unfolded pages.
TABRISI:74:32-56/r14.anchor: وقد جاء عنهم أيضا نشر الله الميت قال المتنبي: ردت صنائعه إليه حياته

TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r1.speaker: المتنبي
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r1.claim: The line's final word ‘unfolded’ supports describing pages as spread out by analogy with the revived dead.
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r1.anchor: فكأنه من نشرها منشور ولم نعلمهم قالوا أنشرت الثوب ونحوه

TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r5.claim: Ṣuḥuf is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, a sheet that can be turned from one side to another because it bears writing; muṣḥaf derives from the same root.
TABRISI:74:32-56#2/r5.anchor: والصحف جمع الصحيفة وهي الورقة التي من شأنها أن تقلب من جهة إلى جهة لما فيها من الكتابة

ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r4.claim: Their demand for separately distributed pages may mean each wants an individually addressed reminder and invitation, perhaps with personalized tasks or benefits, or each wants to be a prophet.
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r4.anchor: her kişi kendisine ayrı ayrı dağıtılmış sahifeler hâlinde tezkire getirilmesini istiyor.

ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r5.claim: They reject a general reminder and imagine that each deserves a separate message like an invitation to a feast, or a personal notice about duties and preparation.
ELMALILI:74:32-56#3/r5.anchor: Umûmî bir tezkire ile iktifâ etmek istemiyor. Her biri ziyafete davet olunur gibi husûsî bir tezkire ile ayrıca davet olunmasını istiyor

NAHHAS:v5p74/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p74/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p74/r7.claim: The feminine singular form reflects the feminine collective, and the singular is used because that form is more numerous.
NAHHAS:v5p74/r7.anchor: على تأنيث الجماعة ووحد لأنه أكثر في العدد

SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r1.claim: The common reading has doubled نشره for منشرة, while Ibn Jubayr reads the lighter form; the common reading also has damma in صحف, while Ibn Jubayr quiesces it.
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r1.anchor: العامة على التشديد من " نشره " بالتضعيف. وابن جبير " منشرة " بالتخفيف

SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r2.claim: The Shaykh says the familiar form with newspapers and cloth is the light triliteral نشر; al-Samin rejects this as a criticism because the doubled reading is canonical.
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r2.anchor: قال الشيخ: " والمحفوظ في الصحيفة والثوب نشر مخففا ثلاثيا " قلت: وهذا مردود بالقرآن المتواتر

SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa explains Ibn Jubayr's reading as ordered to be spread, as already spread, or as made alive by God, so its contents are brought to life by being mentioned.
SAMIN-DURR:74:52/r3.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء في قراءة ابن جبير: " من أنشرت: إما بمعنى أمر بنشرها مثل

ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r1.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r1.claim: They said that a sinner among the Children of Israel would find his sin written on his door the next morning, and asked why they could not receive the same.
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r1.anchor: قيل كانوا يقولون: كان من أذنب من بني إسرائيل يجد ذنبه مكتوبا من غد على بابه فما بالنا لا نكون كذلك.

ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r2.claim: The Qur'an explains their demand elsewhere: they would not believe until a book was sent down for them to read.
ZAJJAJ:v5p250/r2.anchor: وقد جاء في القرآن تفسير طلبهم في سورة بني إسرائيل في قوله: (ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه).

ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r1.claim: Asad glosses the demand as scriptures opened wide, or unfolded so that everyone could understand them.
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r1.anchor: Lit., "everyone of them wants to be given wide-open scriptures", or "scriptures unfolded" (i.e., open to everyone's understanding)

ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r2.claim: Asad compares this demand with 2:118, where people ask for a direct message from God without a prophet's intervention.
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r2.anchor: 2:118 - "Why does not God speak unto us, nor is a message conveyed to us?"

ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r3.claim: Asad calls this the Qur'an's earliest illustration of the arrogance or false pride it frequently condemns.
ASAD-NOTES:74:49#n29/r3.anchor: The above is the earliest illustration of the "arrogance" or "false pride" to which the Qur'an so often refers.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reads "صحفا منشرة" with sukūn on both ḥāʾ and nūn.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r1.anchor: قراءة سعيد بن جبير: "صحفا منشرة3"، بسكون الحاء والنون

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r2.claim: The sukūn on ḥāʾ is a Tamimi dialect form.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r3.claim: The n-sukūn is supported by ordinary usage for spreading cloth and by the expression for God reviving the dead, who then rise.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r3.anchor: فإن جاري العرف في الاستعمال نشرت الثوب ونحوه، ونشر الله الموتى فنشروا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r4.speaker: التيمي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r4.claim: Al-Taymi’s verse says that God’s acts restored life to the dead, who became as if revived; it witnesses the usage of نشر for bringing the dead to life.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r4.anchor: قال التيمي: ردت صنائعه إليه حياته ... فكأنه من نشرها منشورا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r5.claim: Although Arabs are not known to say "أنشرت الثوب", analogy allows a folded sheet to be likened to a dead thing that comes alive when unfolded, hence منشرة.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p340/r5.anchor: أي: كأنها كانت بطيها ميتة، فلما نشرت حيت بذلك، فقيل منشرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r13.claim: They demand individually addressed spread-out pages readable like letters, or pages written in heaven and delivered fresh before folding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r13.anchor: أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة: أي منشورة غير مطوية تقرأ كالكتب التي يتكاتب بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r14.claim: They said each would follow only after receiving a sky-sent book addressed to that individual and ordering belief; a similar demand appears at 17:93.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r14.anchor: أنهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لن نتبعك حتى يؤتى كل واحد منا بكتاب من السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r15.claim: Another report says someone demanded that the records of each person's deeds be shown, and this verse was revealed in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p339/r15.anchor: وروي أن بعضهم قال: إن كان يكتب في صحف ما يعمل كل إنسان، فلتعرض تلك الصحف علينا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r1.claim: The clause is coordinated with an omitted sense supplied by context: they are not satisfied with the admonition and instead demand individual pages.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r1.anchor: عطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام كأنه قيل لا يكتفون بتلك التذكرة ولا يرضون بها بل يريد كل واحد منهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r2.claim: They want each person given scrolls to unroll and read, like letters exchanged between people.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r2.anchor: أن يؤتى قراطيس تنشر وتقرأ كالكتب التي يتكاتب بها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r3.claim: A proposed alternative is books written in heaven and brought by angels, still freshly written and unrolled; al-Ālūsī considers this far-fetched.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يراد كتبا كتبت في السماء ونزلت بها الملائكة ساعة كتبت منشرة على أيديها غضة رطبة لم تطو بعد وفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r4.claim: They reportedly demanded a personal heavenly letter addressed by God to each of them and commanding them to follow the Prophet, paralleling their demand for a book to read.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r4.anchor: إن سرك أن نتابعك فأت كل واحد منا بكتب من السماء عنوانها من رب العالمين إلى فلان بن فلان نؤمر فيها باتباعك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r5.claim: The demand recalls the stated refusal to believe until a readable book descends, and the hypothetical book on parchment they could touch.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r5.anchor: ونحوه قوله تعالى لن نؤمن لك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه قال ولو نزلنا عليك كتابا في قرطاس فلمسوه بأيديهم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r6.claim: Al-Suddī transmits from Abū Ṣāliḥ that they demanded a page under every man’s head by morning, promising exemption and safety from the Fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال قالوا إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح تحت رأسكل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءة وأمنة من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r7.claim: Their precedent was a claim that Israelites awoke with their sin and its expiation written above them; this demand differs from the open, spread pages unless those are understood as exposed writings, yielding the same basic idea.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r7.anchor: وقبل كانوا يقولون بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا على رأسه ذنبه وكفارته

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r8.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the principal interpretation is the demand for the individual heavenly letters, also reported from al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Ibn Zayd.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r8.anchor: فالمعمول عليه ما تقدم وهو مروي عن الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads ṣuḥufan with a still ḥāʾ and munashshara in the lighter form.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير صحفا بإسكان الحاء منشرة بالتخفيف

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r10.claim: For spreading written pages, the triliteral nashara and the form anshara have the same sense, as do anzala and nazzala.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r10.anchor: على أن أنشر الصحف ونشرها واحد كأنزله ونزله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r11.claim: For writing on a scroll or cloth, Arabic uses nashara in the triliteral form; with the dead, God may anshar or nashshar him, meaning revived him and he came alive.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p134#3/r11.anchor: وفي البحر المحفوظ في الصحيفة والثوب نشر مخففا ثلاثيا ويقال في الميت أنشره الله تعالى ونشره ويقال أنشره الله تعالى فنشر هو أي أحياه فحيي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r12.speaker: المفسرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r12.claim: Commentators say Quraysh wanted a revealed book at each man's head each morning confirming Muhammad's mission and commanding obedience.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r12.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن كفار قريش قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلمك ليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا كتاب منشور من الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r13.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r13.claim: Al-Kalbī says they cited an Israelite who woke with sin and expiation written at his head, asking Muhammad for the same.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r13.anchor: قال الكلبي: إن المشركين قالوا: يا محمد بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r14.claim: Ṣuḥuf are books, plural of ṣaḥīfah; munashsharah means spread open.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p274/r14.anchor: الصحف" الكتب، وهي جمع الصحيفة، و"منشرة" منشورة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r3.claim: The spread-out scrolls are sheets that can be unfolded and read.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r4.claim: The Quraysh said they would not follow the Prophet until each received a book from heaven addressed by God to that individual and commanding him to follow Muhammad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:50-56/r4.anchor: وذلك أنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كلامنا بكتاب من السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r3.claim: They told the Prophet they would not follow until each received an open book from heaven addressed by God to that person and commanding him to follow Muhammad.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r3.anchor: قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كلا منا بكتاب من السماء فيه : من الله إلى فلان اتبع محمدا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r4.claim: The scrolls are many, each spread open and unobstructed for reading and taking.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r4.anchor: قراطيس مكتوبة { منشرة * } أي كثيرة جدا وكل واحد منها منشور لا مانع

BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r5.claim: Kalla rejects the proposed condition: they have no genuine intention to follow, whether or not they receive these documents.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p238/r5.anchor: ليس لهم غرض في الاتباع بوجه من الوجوه لا بهذا الشرط ولا بغيره

DURR-FULL:v8p339/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r16.speaker: السدي عن أبي صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r16.claim: Some Quraysh demanded a personal written guarantee of release and safety from Hell beneath every man's head; this demand occasioned the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p339/r16.anchor: عن السدي عن أبي صالح قال: قالوا: إن كان محمدا صادقا فليصبح تحت رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة

DURR-FULL:v8p340/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r1.claim: Mujahid says each wanted a sheet addressed to him by name from the Lord of the worlds, placed at his head for reading.
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه {بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة} قال: إلى فلان بن فلان من رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v8p340/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r2.claim: Qatada says people told Muhammad that they would follow him if he brought them a private book ordering them to do so.
DURR-FULL:v8p340/r2.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة} قال: قد قال قائلون من الناس لمحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r12.speaker: أبو جهل وعبد الله بن أبي أمية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r12.claim: Abū Jahl, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Umayya, and other Quraysh unbelievers demanded a personal document from God addressed to each man, as another tactic for denying revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p330/r12.anchor: إضراب انتقالي لذكر حالة أخرى من أحوال عنادهم إذ قال أبو جهل وعبد الله بن أبي أمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r1.claim: The plural may mean that every command or prohibition for each person would need its own separate document.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r1.anchor: إما لأنهم سألوا أن يكون كل أمر أو نهي تأتي الواحد منهم في شأنه صحيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r2.claim: Alternatively, because they jointly demanded a named document for each man, the collection is described as if all those documents came to every individual.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r2.anchor: وإما لأنهم لما سألوا أن تأتي كل واحد منهم صحيفة باسمه وكانوا جماعة متفقين جمع لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r3.claim: Munashshara means unrolled, open, and readable; they reject a folded document whose contents they cannot see, and the intensive form stresses its being unfolded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r3.anchor: أي لا نكتفي بصحيفة مطوية لا نعلم ما كتب فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r4.claim: The author cites the report about the stoning to show the verb’s use: they opened the Torah.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r5.claim: Kallā rejects and rebukes the apparent demand: they will not receive such documents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p331/r5.anchor: وردع عن ذلك ، أي لا يكون لهم ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r12.claim: The opponents demand that each person receive a book sent down to him by God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r12.anchor: معناه من هؤلاء المعارضين، أي يريد كل إنسان منهم أن ينزل عليه كتاب من الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أمية وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r13.claim: The demand was attributed to Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya and others.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r13.anchor: وكان هذا من قول عبد الله بن أبي أمية وغيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r14.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r14.claim: Some objectors reportedly said that if each person's deeds were written in sheets, those sheets should be presented to them for inspection; the verse was then revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r14.anchor: وروي أن بعضهم قال إن كان يكتب في صحف ما يعمل كل إنسان فلتعرض ذلك الصحف علينا فنزلت الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r15.claim: منشرة means spread open rather than folded.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r16.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r16.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads صحفا with a still ḥāʾ, a Yemeni dialect form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p399/r16.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير «صحفا» بسكون الحاء وهي لغة يمانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r1.claim: A reading has منشرة with a still nūn and a light shīn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r2.claim: The form is explained by comparing a spread garment with God raising the dead; al-Taymi reverses the comparison in a poem. Ordinary usage is نشرت الصحيفة and أنشر الله الميت, though نشر الله الميت is also attested.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p400/r2.anchor: وهذا على أن يشبه نشرت الثوب بأنشر الله الميت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r1.claim: The majority say the Quraysh demanded that every man receive an open book from God at his bedside, addressed to him by name and commanding him to follow Muhammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r1.anchor: أحدها أنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إن سرك أن نتبعك فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا كتاب منشور من الله تعالى إلى فلان بن فلان يؤمر فيه باتباعك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r2.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r2.claim: Abu Salih says they wanted a written guarantee of release from the Fire and freedom from its punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r2.anchor: والثاني أنهم أرادوا براءة من النار أن لا يعذبوا بها قاله أبو صالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r3.claim: Al-Farra says they invoked Israelites, who found their sins written on a slip by morning, and asked why they did not see such records; the response is that they will not receive the scrolls.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r3.anchor: والثالث أنهم قالوا كان الرجل إذا أذنب في بني إسرائيل وجده مكتوبا إذا أصبح في رقعة فما بالنا لا نرى ذلك فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r4.claim: The verse answers that they will not be given the scrolls they demand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p413/r4.anchor: فقال الله تعالى كلا أي لا يؤتون الصحف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r5.claim: Mujahid and others say each polytheist wants a book revealed to him as the Prophet’s was.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r5.anchor: أي: بل يريد كل واحد من هؤلاء المشركين أن ينزل عليه كتابا كما أنزل على النبي. قاله مجاهد وغيره،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r6.claim: Their demand resembles those who refuse belief until they receive what God gave His messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r6.anchor: كقوله: {وإذا جاءتهم آية قالوا لن نؤمن حتى نؤتى مثل ما أوتي رسل الله الله أعلم حيث يجعل رسالته}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r7.claim: In another report, Qatada says they want acquittal without doing any deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273#2/r7.anchor: وفي رواية عن قتادة: يريدون أن يؤتوا براءة بغير عمل.

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r8.claim: Ṣaḥīfa has plurals ṣuḥuf and ṣaḥāʾif; muṣḥaf derives from it and has plural maṣāḥif.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r8.anchor: والصحيفة: جمعه صحف وصحائف، ومنه: المصحف، وجمعه: المصاحف.

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r9.claim: Nashr is opposite folding: spreading out something wrapped.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r9.anchor: والنشر: خلاف الطي، وهو بسط الملتف.

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r13.speaker: الحسن وقتادة ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r13.claim: They say polytheists would follow Muhammad if he brought individual letters from God to named leaders affirming that they should follow him.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r13.anchor: نؤمن فيها باتباعك، عن الحسن، وقتادة، ومجاهد.

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says polytheists demanded a sheet at each person's head certifying deliverance from the Fire if Muhammad was truthful.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r14.anchor: فليصبح عند رأس كل أحد منا صحيفة فيها براءة من النار، فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r15.speaker: مطر الوراق
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r15.claim: Matar al-Warrāq says they wanted exemption without any deeds.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r15.anchor: قال مطر الوراق: كانوا يريدون براءة من غير عمل،

JISHUMI:v10p7170/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r16.claim: Another account says they asked for sheets listing each person's sin and expiation as with the Israelites; the Prophet disliked the demand and the verse was revealed.
JISHUMI:v10p7170/r16.anchor: وقيل: قالوا: يا محمد، بلغنا أن بني إسرائيل كانوا إذا أذنب واحد منهم أصبح وعند رأسه مكتوب

JISHUMI:v10p7173/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7173/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7173/r5.claim: Desire for what will not occur is genuine willing, not mere wishing, contrary to opponents.
JISHUMI:v10p7173/r5.anchor: أن الكافر يريد ما لا يكون، وإرادة ما لا يكون إرادة، وليست بتمن، خلاف قولهم [*].

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r11.claim: The scattered sheets can be open papers or letters like those people exchange, or heavenly books newly written and brought by angels, still fresh and unfolded.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r11.anchor: قراطيس تنشر وقرأ كالكتب التي يتكاتب بها أو كتبا كتبت في السماء ونزلت بها الملائكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r12.claim: They demanded that each person receive a heavenly document addressed by God by name and commanding him to follow the Messenger; the same demand appears elsewhere.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r12.anchor: لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا بكتب من السماء عنوانها من رب العالمين إلى فلان بن فلان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r13.claim: Another report of their demand is that every man wake to find a sheet declaring his innocence and safety from the Fire.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : قالوا إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءته وأمنه من النار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r14.claim: They also invoked a claim about Israelites waking to find their sin and expiation written above them; al-Zamakhsharī says this is remote from the phrase unless it means publicly exposed writings.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r14.anchor: بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا على رأسه ذنبه وكفارته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r15.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r15.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads both words with light consonants; anshara and nashara have the same sense, like anzala and nazzala.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير : ( صحفا منشرة ) بتخفيفهما ، على أن أنشر الصحف ونشرها : واحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r16.claim: Kallā rejects their wish for extraordinary documents and rebukes them for demanding signs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p657#2/r16.anchor: ردعهم بقوله { كلا } عن تلك الإرادة ، وزجرهم عن اقتراح الآيات ، ثم قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.speaker: رسول الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds for each person in Mecca who believed in Muhammad or disbelieved in him to whoever recites al-Muddaththir; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p658/r3.anchor: من قرأ سورة المدثر أعطاه الله عشر حسنات بعدد من صدق بمحمد وكذب به بمكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r8.claim: The unfolded pages are books spread open.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r9.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r9.claim: Qatada says each person wanted a book from God commanding him to believe in Muhammad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r9.anchor: أن يؤتى كتابا من الله أن يؤمن بمحمد , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r10.claim: Abu Salih says each wanted a guarantee from the Fire that he would not be cast into it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r10.anchor: أن يؤتى براءة من النار أنه لا يقذف بها , قاله أبو صالح

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r11.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r11.claim: Muqatil says each wanted a book from God listing what was permitted and prohibited for him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r11.anchor: أن يؤتى كتابا من الله بما أحل له وحرم عليه , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r12.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r12.claim: Al-Farraʾ says Quraysh objected that Israelites could see each person's sins written on a sheet and asked why they could not; the verse was revealed in response.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p148/r12.anchor: أن كفار قريش قالوا إن بني إسرائيل كانوا إذا أذنب الواحد ذنبا وجده مكتوبا في رقعة , فما بالنا لا نرى ذلك فنزلت الآية , قاله الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r1.speaker: العلماء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r1.claim: When a jurist finds two rulings or meanings equally supported, one scholarly view lets the jurist choose either.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون مخيرا ، للعمل في العمل على أيهما شاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r2.speaker: العلماء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r2.claim: The other scholarly view requires choosing the ruling that is stricter.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r2.anchor: والضرب الثاني : أن يأخذ بأغلظ المذهبين حكما

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r3.claim: For another kind of difference, where meanings do not conflict and can be combined, the meanings may both be intended.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r3.anchor: من اختلاف المعنيين : ألا يتنافيا ويمكن الجمع بينهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r4.claim: When compatible meanings are equally supported and neither is preferred by evidence, both are intended; otherwise God would have supplied evidence to specify only one.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r5.claim: A single expression encompassing two compatible meanings is more eloquent than expressing each meaning in separate wording.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r5.anchor: جاز أن يريدهما بلف واحد ، يشتمل عليهما ، ويكون ذلك أبلغ في الإعجاز والفصاحة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r6.claim: If evidence disproves one of two meanings, that meaning and its ruling fall away, leaving the other as intended and operative.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r6.anchor: على بطلان أحد المعنيين ، فيسقط حكمهن ويصير المعنى الآخر هو المراد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r7.claim: Evidence supporting one meaning without invalidating the other establishes the first but does not exclude the second, which remains possible through the wording itself.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r7.anchor: أن يكون دليلا على صحة أحد المعنيين فيثبت حكمه ويكون مرادا ولا يقتضي سقوط المعنى الآخر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r8.claim: Some scholars hold that the meaning supported by evidence has stronger status than a meaning lacking separate evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r8.anchor: وذهب بعض أهل العلم إلى أن المعنى الذي يرجح بدليل أثبت حكما من المعنى الذي تجرد عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r9.claim: Al-Māwardī presents this method as a basis for evaluating the multiple meanings Qur'anic wording can bear and deciding which meanings to apply or set aside.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r9.anchor: ليكون ما احتمله ألفاظ القرآن من اختلاف المعاني

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r10.claim: The Prophet is reported to say every revealed verse has an outward and inward sense, each letter a limit, and each limit a place of ascent; al-Māwardī identifies it as an āḥād report.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r10.anchor: ما نزل القرآن من آية إلا لها ظهر وبطن ولكل حرف حد ولكل حد مطلع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r11.claim: Al-Māwardī says the reported hadith does not conflict with his interpretive principles because it admits different interpretations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p40/r11.anchor: منافيا لما قررناه من الأصول المستمرة ، لما فيه من التأويلات المختلفة

BURSEVI:v10p187/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p187/r10.claim: Instead of accepting the reminder, they stubbornly demand separate heavenly books for every person; Abu Jahl, Abdullah ibn Umayya, and their companions made this demand of the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v10p187/r10.anchor: عطف على مقدر يقتضيه المقام كأنه قيل لا يكلفون بتلك التذكرة

BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r1.speaker: أبو جهل وعبد الله بن أمية وأصحابهما
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r1.claim: They demanded a separate page from the Lord of the worlds addressed to each person and ordering him to follow Muhammad; they also said they would not believe without a book to read.
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r1.anchor: عنوانها من رب العالمين إلى فلان ابن فلا تؤمر فيها باتباعك أي بأن يقال اتبع محمدا فإنه رسول من قبلي إليك

BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r2.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r2.claim: Al-Qamus defines marʾ as a human being or man and gives three forms of its initial hamza and case behavior; it has no plural from the same lexical form.
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r2.anchor: في "القاموس" المرء مثلثة الميم الإنسان أو الرجل

BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r3.claim: In the clause, an-na with its complement is the first object of yuridu, the pronoun in yu'ta is the first object of that verb, and suhuf is its second object; munashshara describes suhuf.
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r3.anchor: وأن مع صلته مفعول يريد وصحفا مفعول ثان ليؤتى والأول ضمير كل ومنتشرة صفة صحف

BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r4.speaker: تاج المصادر
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r4.claim: Taj al-Masadir says the doubled form munashshara marks abundance or multiplicity.
BURSEVI:v10p187#2/r4.anchor: قال في تاج المصادر وصحف منتشرة شدد للكثرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r1.claim: They want individually delivered sheets that can be unfolded and read.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r1.anchor: قراطيس تنشر وتقرأ وذلك انهم قالوا لرسول الله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r2.claim: They told the Messenger they would not follow unless each received a heavenly letter addressed by name and commanding belief in him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r2.anchor: وذلك انهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لن نتبعك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا يكتب من السماء عنوانها من رب العالمين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r3.claim: Another report says they demanded a sheet at each man's head certifying his innocence and safety from Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r3.anchor: وقيل قالوا ان كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءته وأمنه من النار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r4.claim: The demand for a book to read is like the demand in 17:93.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p298#11/r4.anchor: ونحوه قوله لن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل عليها كتابا نقرؤه

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r1.claim: The open pages mean opened books; Abu Jahl and Quraysh demanded written certification from God that Muhammad had been sent, like the demand in 17:93.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r1.anchor: وذلك أن أبا جهل وجماعة من قريش قالوا: يا محمد! ايتنا بكتب من رب العالمين مكتوب فيها: إني قد أرسلت

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they wanted every man to wake to a page guaranteeing his acquittal and safety from the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كانوا يقولون إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءته وأمنه من النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r3.speaker: مطر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r3.claim: Matar al-Warraq says they wanted to be given this without doing deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r3.anchor: قال مطر الوراق: أرادوا أن يعطوا بغير عمل.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r4.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi says they compared themselves to Israelites who supposedly found their sins and expiation written at their heads each morning.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قال المشركون: بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r5.claim: Mujahid says each person wanted a book addressed by God to him by name.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أرادوا أن ينزل على كل واحد منهم كتاب فيه من الله عز وجل: إلى فلان بن فلان.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r6.claim: Another view takes the pages as a metaphor for being mentioned with praise; the pages stand for remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أن يذكر بذكر جميل، فجعلت الصحف موضع الذكر مجازا.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r7.claim: They objected that if human sins are written down, they should be able to see the writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r7.anchor: وقالوا: إذا كانت ذنوب الإنسان تكتب عليه فما بالنا لا نرى ذلك؟

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r10.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reads suhuf with silent ha and munashshara with silent nun; the ha is lightened, while the nun reading is anomalous.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r10.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير «صحفا منشرة» بسكون الحاء والنون، فأما تسكين الحاء فتخفيف، وأما النون فشاذ.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r11.claim: The usual verb nashara applies to spreading cloth, not anshara; alternatively, a folded page is like a dead thing revived when opened.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:52-53/r11.anchor: إنما يقال: نشرت الثوب وشبهه ولا يقال أنشرت. ويجوز أن يكون شبه الصحيفة بالميت كأنها ميتة بطيها، فإذا نشرت حييت

RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r1.claim: They demanded that each person receive a sky-sent book addressed to him by name and commanding him to follow the Messenger, paralleling another demand for a readable book from heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r1.anchor: أنهم قالوا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لا نؤمن بك حتى تأتي كل واحد منا بكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r2.claim: Another account says they wanted a written book on parchment that they could touch with their hands.
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r2.anchor: ونظيره { لن نؤمن * لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرءه }

RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r3.claim: Some said they wanted each man to wake with a page declaring him safe from the Fire.
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح عند رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءة من النار

RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r4.claim: They also cited a report that an Israelite woke with his sin and its expiation written on his head; al-Razi says this is far from “pages spread out” unless that means openly displayed writing.
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r4.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يقولون بلغنا أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل كان يصبح مكتوبا على رأسه ذنبه وكفارته

RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reads both words with the lighter forms, since spreading and causing to spread are equivalent, like the paired forms anzala/nazzala.
RAZI-FULL:v30p187/r5.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير { صحفا منشرة } بتخفيفهما على أن أنشر الصحف ونشرها واحد

STUDYQURAN:74:52/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r1.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r1.claim: Each man wants a revelation addressed directly to him, like those who ask why God does not speak to them or send them a sign.
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r1.anchor: Each man wants a revelation that is addressed directly to him (Q, Ṭ), as in 2:118

STUDYQURAN:74:52/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r2.speaker: some of the Quraysh
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r2.claim: Some Quraysh objected that, if Muhammad were truly God’s Messenger, he could give each of them a book granting exemption and protection from the Fire.
STUDYQURAN:74:52/r2.anchor: It is also reported that some of the Quraysh objected by saying that, if Muhammad were truly a Messenger of God, he could bring a book that would give each of them exemption

TAB-FULL:v23p461/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r1.claim: Their refusal is not from ignorance that the Qurʾān is from God; each wants a personal book sent down from heaven.
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r1.anchor: ولكن كل رجل منهم يريد أن يؤتى كتابا من السماء

TAB-FULL:v23p461/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r2.claim: Qatāda reports that they demanded a private written order for named individuals to follow Muhammad.
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة}

TAB-FULL:v23p461/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r3.claim: Qatāda characterizes their wish as wanting a declaration of acquittal with no deeds.
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: يريدون أن يؤتوا براءة بغير عمل

TAB-FULL:v23p461/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r4.claim: Mujāhid paraphrases the demand as a scroll from the Lord of the worlds addressed to each individual.
TAB-FULL:v23p461/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منشرة}

SULAMI:v2p359#7/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p359#7/r1.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p359#7/r1.claim: Al-Ḥusayn asks how people empty of Truth, turned from its concerns, and heedless of standing before Him could understand the opened pages and their hidden secrets.
SULAMI:v2p359#7/r1.anchor: قال الحسين : كيف لهم بهذه الإرادة ولهم نفوس خالية من الحق معرضة عن أمور الحق

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.claim: After the preceding threat and promise, the passage presents as astonishing the rejection of the Qur'an's reminder and recoil from manifest truth: they should believe, yet seek individual revelation instead.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r1.anchor: في معنى الاستنتاج مما تقدم من الوعيد والوعد أورد في صورة التعجب من إعراضهم عن تذكرة القرآن

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r5.claim: The spread pages are a heavenly scripture containing the true call.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r5.anchor: المراد بالصحف المنشرة الكتاب السماوي المشتمل على الدعوة الحقة

TABATABAI:74:49-52/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r6.claim: The shift explains that aversion is not mere flight: each wants a separate book from God containing the Qur'an's message, a demand that implies arrogance toward God and refusal of a truthful messenger despite clear signs.
TABATABAI:74:49-52/r6.anchor: ليس إعراضهم عن التذكرة لمجرد النفرة بل يريد كل امرئ منهم أن ينزل عليه كتاب من عند الله

TABATABAI:74:53/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:53/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:53/r1.claim: The demand resembles their statement that they would not believe until given what God's messengers were given, and the analogous argument of earlier peoples against messengers as mere humans.
TABATABAI:74:53/r1.anchor: وفي معنى قول الأمم لرسلهم { إن أنتم إلا بشر مثلنا } على ما قررنا من حجتهم

TABATABAI:74:53/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:53/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:53/r2.claim: One view relates the verse to their demand that the Prophet ascend to heaven and bring down a book for them to read; al-Tabataba'i rejects it because 74:52 asks for separate pages for each person, unlike the single book in 17:93.
TABATABAI:74:53/r2.anchor: وقيل إن الآية في معنى قولهم للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الذي حكاه الله في قوله ولن نؤمن لرقيك

TABATABAI:74:53/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:53/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:53/r3.claim: Another proposed meaning is that books bearing each person's name would descend from heaven and command belief in Muhammad; the author finds this and related proposals contextually remote.
TABATABAI:74:53/r3.anchor: وقيل المراد نزول كتب من السماء عليهم بأسمائهم أن آمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:74:53/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:53/r4.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:53/r4.claim: A further view says they wanted books absolving them from punishment and granting blessings before they would believe; al-Tabataba'i rejects it as remote from the context.
TABATABAI:74:53/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد أن ينزل عليهم كتب من السماء بالبراءة من العذاب وإسباغ النعمة

TABATABAI:74:53/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:53/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:53/r5.claim: He dismisses these proposals as far from the context and relies on the earlier reading: each demands an individual heavenly book.
TABATABAI:74:53/r5.anchor: وهي جميعا معان بعيدة من السياق والتعويل على ما تقدم

TABRISI:74:49-56/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:74:49-56/r7.claim: They say each person wants a heavenly book addressed to him by name, commanding belief in Muḥammad.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r7.anchor: تنزل إليهم بأسمائهم أن آمنوا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الحسن وقتادة وابن زيد

TABRISI:74:49-56/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:49-56/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that they demand written guarantees against punishment and promises of blessing even while persisting in disbelief.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r8.anchor: يريدون صحفا من الله تعالى بالبراءة من العقوبة وإسباغ النعمة

TABRISI:74:49-56/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:49-56/r9.claim: Another view says each wants to be a prophet receiving revelation and having followers, refusing to be a follower.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r9.anchor: يريد كل واحد منهم أن يكون رسولا يوحى إليه متبوعا وأنف من أن يكون تابعا

TABRISI:74:49-56/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:49-56/r10.claim: The demand for written pages explains their earlier demand for a book from heaven to read.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r10.anchor: ولن نؤمن لرقيك حتى تنزل علينا كتابا نقرؤه

TABRISI:74:49-56/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:49-56/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:49-56/r11.claim: Kallā rejects their demand: events will not happen as they propose.
TABRISI:74:49-56/r11.anchor: أي حقا ليس الأمر على ما قالوا ولا يكون كذلك

FARRA:v3p205/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p205/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p205/r9.claim: Quraysh objected that sinners among the Israelites woke to find their sins written on a slip and asked why they did not see such pages; the verse answers that each wants pages spread before him.
FARRA:v3p205/r9.anchor: قالت كفار قريش للنبي صلى الله عليه [114/ ا] : كان الرجل يذنب في بني إسرائيل، فيصبح ذنبه مكتوبا في رقعة، فما بالنا لا نرى ذلك؟

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#4/r1.speaker: كفار قريش
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#4/r1.claim: Quraysh's unbelievers said that if a man's sin were recorded on a sheet, they could not understand why they did not see such a record themselves.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p498#4/r1.anchor: قالت كفار قريش: "إن كان الرجل يذنب، فيكتب ذنبه في رقعة:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r1.speaker: المفسرون، ومجاهد، ومقاتل، وقتادة، والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r1.claim: Quraysh demanded a separate revealed book at each man’s head declaring their idols false, God true, and Muhammad His messenger, with orders to follow him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬1): وذلك أن كفار قريش قالوا لمحمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ليصبح عند رأس كل منا كتاب منشور من الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says Quraysh invoked an Israelite custom: after sinning, a man woke to a written record of his sin and its remedy, and they would believe if given such pages.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: إنهم قالوا: كنا نحدث أن الرجل من بني إسرائيل إذا أذنب ذنبا أصبح وعند رأسه صحيفة مكتوبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r3.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj prefer al-Kalbi’s explanation: plural pages suit a separate page for each man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r3.anchor: وهو اختيار # الفراء (¬1) , والزجاج (¬2)) (¬3)؛ ويدل على صحته (¬4) قوله: {صحفا منشرة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r4.claim: Ṣuḥuf means books, and its singular is ṣaḥīfa.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r5.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r5.claim: Al-Layth notes the rare plural pattern fuʿul for faʿīla, as in safīna/sufun; the expected forms are ṣaḥāʾif and safāʾin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r5.anchor: قال الليث: ومن النوادر أن تجمع فعيلة على فعل، مثل سفينة وسفن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r6.claim: Munashshara means spread out or published; the intensive form indicates abundance in the distribution.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p464/r6.anchor: و {منشرة} معناها منشورة، والتفعيل (¬7) للكثرة في الجمع.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r5.claim: Each person demanded a separate book from the Lord of the worlds ordering him to follow the Prophet, echoing their demand for a book to read.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:49-56/r5.anchor: بل يريد كل امرىء منهم أن يؤتى صحفا منتشرة } وذلك أنهم قالوا: إن سرك أن نتبعك فأت كل واحد منا بكتاب من رب العالمين نؤمر فيه باتباعك

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r2.speaker: Ebû Cehil ve yandaşları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r2.claim: Commentaries report that Abu Jahl and a group demanded a written divine document addressed to each of them ordering them to follow the Prophet, and said they would not believe without it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r2.anchor: Tefsirlerde anlatıldığına göre Ebû Cehil ve yandaşlarından bir grup Hz. Peygamber’e hitaben, “Allah’tan, her birimizin adına yazılmış olup sana tâbi olmamızı emreden bir kitap, bir belge getirmedikçe sana iman etmeyiz” demişlerdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r3.claim: Verse 52 voices their demand for individual written documents from God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:49/r3.anchor: 52. âyet onların bu isteklerini dile getirmektedir (Zemahşerî, IV, 188; İbn Âşûr, XXIX, 331).

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224/r3.speaker: السدي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says Quraysh demanded a guarantee of safety from the Fire in a page placed under each man's head every morning; this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن السدي قال قالوا لئن كان محمد صادقا فليصبح تحت رأس كل رجل منا صحيفة فيها براءة وأمنة من النار

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.claim: Kallā is rebuke and restraint: it tells people to stop, denies a preceding claim, or rejects their conduct.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p295#2/r1.anchor: كلا: ردع وزجر، قال الله تعالى: أيطمع كل امرئ منهم أن يدخل جنة نعيم
